questions.q: What problem does the self-hosted integration runtime actually solve?
options: Reaching data sources inside a private network that the Azure IR can't connect to
Replacing the Azure IR entirely in every data factory
Making Copy activities run faster than the Azure IR
Running SSIS packages, which the Azure IR can't do
questions.explain: The Azure IR lives in Azure's own network and has no path into an on-premises or private network — the self-hosted IR is software you install inside that network specifically to bridge the gap.

questions.q: What does a self-hosted integration runtime actually consist of?
options: A managed Azure VM that Microsoft provisions for you automatically
The Microsoft Integration Runtime Configuration Manager, installed on a machine you control
A browser extension installed on the developer's laptop
A SQL Server stored procedure
questions.explain: It's real software — the Configuration Manager — installed and registered on a Windows machine inside your own network, not a managed Azure resource.

questions.q: What does a self-hosted IR use to register itself against a specific data factory?
options: It registers automatically with no credential at all
The data factory's admin password
A self-signed SSL certificate you create manually
An authentication key generated when the IR is created
questions.explain: Data Factory generates a primary and secondary authentication key when you create the self-hosted IR; pasting one into the Configuration Manager registers that node.

questions.q: Why would a self-hosted integration runtime have more than one node?
options: Each node must belong to a different data factory
Nodes have nothing to do with availability — they're purely cosmetic
For high availability and greater scalability for data movement
Because a single node can only run one pipeline at a time
questions.explain: Multiple nodes (up to four) share one logical self-hosted IR, keeping data movement running if one node goes down and adding throughput — Microsoft recommends at least two for production.

questions.q: In the self-hosted IR architecture, which side initiates the network connection?
options: Azure Data Factory initiates an inbound connection into the corporate network
Neither side initiates — it's a peer-to-peer connection
The self-hosted IR initiates an outbound connection to Azure
The on-premises data source connects directly to Azure, bypassing the IR
questions.explain: The self-hosted IR always initiates outbound, so no inbound port has to be opened into the corporate network — Lesson 37 covers exactly what that requires from a firewall.
